minutes.headline: Sewer Commission moved to require new hookups tie into the line on their own addressed street
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Sewer Commission approved prior minutes, reviewed ADU (accessory dwelling unit) regulations and easement language pending town counsel guidance, and heard a billing update showing a large share of second-quarter FY26 sewer bills still unpaid along with FY25 unpaid bills going onto tax liens. The main forward-looking item was a plan to bring a proposed regulation to the spring special town meeting requiring new sewer connections to tie into the line on the street the property is actually addressed to, prompted by a recent Chestnut Street construction dispute, to be paired with the ADU rule changes.

what_happened.line: The Commission will bring a proposed rule to the spring special town meeting requiring new sewer hookups to tie into the line on the street the property is actually addressed to.
That regulation will be prepped alongside pending ADU (accessory dwelling unit) rule changes, both headed to town counsel before the meeting.
The tie-in rule follows a recent dispute over a Chestnut Street sewer connection.
The business manager reported a large share of this quarter's sewer bills still unpaid, with unpaid FY25 balances going onto property tax liens.
No votes were taken beyond approving prior minutes and adjourning.

why_it_matters: A new sewer-connection rule tying hookups to a property's addressed street would affect anyone building or connecting near a lot line where two streets have sewer mains, and it goes to a town meeting vote in the spring.
Unpaid sewer bills that convert to tax liens attach to the property, not just the account, so residents behind on sewer charges could see that debt show up on their tax bill.
ADU regulation and easement language, still pending town counsel review, will shape what accessory dwelling units are allowed to do about sewer access.
